title: Place value notes
summary: These notes explain how each digit in a number has a place that says what it is worth. They cover reading numbers like 345 as 300 + 40 + 5, comparing numbers place by place, and regrouping 10 of one place into 1 of the next.

key_ideas.title: Each digit has a place
key_ideas.explanation: Where a digit sits in a number tells you what it is worth — hundreds, tens or ones.

key_ideas.title: Expanded form
key_ideas.explanation: A number can be written as the sum of what each digit is worth, like 345 = 300 + 40 + 5.

key_ideas.title: Comparing numbers
key_ideas.explanation: To see which number is bigger, compare digits starting at the biggest place, not the ones place.

key_ideas.title: Regrouping
key_ideas.explanation: Ten of one place makes one of the next place up — 10 ones is 1 ten, 10 tens is 1 hundred.
